claims.title: Binary edit codes: uniform alignment-count bound and paid signed-syndrome selection

quoted_fields.interface: Binary equal-length words of length n, integer1<=t<=floor(n/4). Canonical alignments have d deletions,d insertions,s substitutions with2d+s<=2t. For the syndrome operation, an explicitly constructed affine hash H and its collision-witness family supply L(S)=|S|-W_H(S), L(all)>=2^(n-1), and exact affine-prefix counts. Counts can be signed; children need not both be nonnegative. Fixed-t source construction/decoding contracts are retained, not strengthened into a uniform growing-t theorem.
quoted_fields.failure: Complete count/existence and paid prefix-selection operations only. The leading2 entropy-scale redundancy bound is not a polynomial-uniform construction for growing t. Randomized document-exchange guarantees for words independent of sketch randomness do not automatically give a single fixed adversarial binary code; deterministic conversion’s extra log(n/t) is retained. Existing fixed-t affine/counting/candidate-decoding machinery is mature imported capital, counted once. No new impact grade, practical code or full negative is assigned. Every known/unknown source/access/transfer hold remains. Hypothetical compressed counts and whole-coset reconstruction are SUFFICIENT, not proven necessary. Whole-coset off-promise recovery may be stronger than a code decoder needs; pointwise isolation is stronger than codebook distance. Standard BCH is substitutions only.
